// A sibling `tests.rs`: every fn here is test code.
// path-stubs: rawtool — the EnvGuard swaps below put a hand-built `rawtool` on PATH
use super::*;
use std::env::set_var as sv;

const PATH_VAR: &str = "PATH";
const OTHER_VAR: &str = "HOME";

#[test]
#[serial_test::serial(path_env)]
fn a_keyed_stub_test_is_not_reported() {
    let tools = FakeToolDir::new();
    tools.tool("faketool").install();
    let _path = tools.activate();
}

#[test]
fn an_unkeyed_stub_test_is_reported() {
    let tools = FakeToolDir::new();
    let _path = tools.activate();
}

#[test]
#[serial(stub_counter)]
fn a_stub_test_under_another_key_is_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set("PATH", "/stub");
}

#[test]
#[serial(stub_counter, path_env)]
fn a_second_key_beside_path_env_is_not_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set(
        "PATH",
        "/stub",
    );
}

#[test]
#[serial(
    path_env,
)]
fn a_key_spelled_over_several_lines_is_not_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set("PATH", "/stub");
}

// `file_serial` locks per file and never meets a `serial(path_env)` test in
// another file of the binary.
#[test]
#[file_serial(path_env)]
fn a_file_serial_key_is_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set("PATH", "/stub");
}

#[test]
#[cfg_attr(
    windows,
    ignore = "no stub on windows"
)]
fn a_test_behind_a_multi_line_attribute_is_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set("PATH", "/stub");
}

#[test]
/* the block comment between the attribute and the item is not the item */
fn a_test_behind_a_block_comment_is_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::remove("PATH");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn an_async_test_is_reported() {
    unsafe { set_var("PATH", "/stub") };
}

#[rstest]
fn an_rstest_test_is_reported() {
    unsafe { remove_var("PATH") };
}

#[test_case(1)]
fn a_test_case_test_is_reported() {
    unsafe {
        set_var(
            "PATH",
            "/stub",
        )
    };
}

#[test]
fn an_aliased_set_var_is_reported() {
    unsafe { sv("PATH", "/stub") };
}

#[test]
fn a_const_naming_path_is_reported() {
    let _path = EnvGuard::set(PATH_VAR, "/stub");
}

#[test]
fn a_let_naming_path_is_reported() {
    let key = "PATH";
    let _path = EnvGuard::set(key, "/stub");
}

#[test]
fn a_const_naming_another_variable_is_not_reported() {
    let _home = EnvGuard::set(OTHER_VAR, "/h");
}

#[test]
fn an_unresolvable_name_is_reported_as_a_variable() {
    let _guard = EnvGuard::set(key_from_elsewhere(), "/x");
}

#[test]
fn an_unresolvable_name_with_a_reason_is_not_reported() {
    // not-path: the key is the fixture's own counter variable
    let _guard = EnvGuard::set(key_from_elsewhere(), "/x");
}

macro_rules! stub_test {
    ($name:ident) => {
        #[test]
        fn $name() {
            let _path = FakeToolDir::new().activate();
        }
    };
}

// A helper is derived from its body, and so is a helper that calls one.
fn stub_absent() -> PathGuard {
    FakeToolDir::new().activate()
}

fn stub_absent_twice() -> PathGuard {
    stub_absent()
}

// No test calls this one.
fn stub_nobody_calls() -> PathGuard {
    FakeToolDir::new().activate()
}

#[test]
fn a_test_swapping_through_a_helper_is_reported() {
    let _path = stub_absent();
}

#[test]
fn a_test_swapping_through_a_helper_of_a_helper_is_reported() {
    let _path = stub_absent_twice();
}

#[test]
fn a_test_swapping_through_a_core_helper_is_reported() {
    let _path = core_stub();
}

// Neither of these swaps PATH: another variable, and the spelling quoted.
#[test]
fn another_variable_is_not_reported() {
    let _home = EnvGuard::set("HOME", "/h");
    let _text = "tools.activate() and EnvGuard::set(\"PATH\", x)";
}

#[test]
fn reads_the_stubbed_tool() {}

#[test]
#[serial_test::serial(path_env)]
fn reads_the_stubbed_tool_keyed() {}

// path-ok: the verdict is the same whichever of the two it ran.
#[test]
fn reads_the_stubbed_tool_marked() {}

#[test]
fn reads_the_raw_tool() {}

#[test]
fn reads_nothing() {}
